title: Consolidated Landing Zones & Predictive Route Tiles
creator: Marco Liu
description: Redesign the console entry experience by introducing consolidated landing zones (role-aware entry points) and a predictive route-tile system that surfaces contextual destinations (dashboards, rollouts, cost views, model monitor). The goal is: reduce task time-to-destination, surface high-value actions (canary rollouts, cost breakdowns), and provide a single adaptable canvas for quick switching across workspaces and environments. Key behaviours: 1) landing zones adapt to user role and recent activity (e.g., platform engineer sees capacity dashboards, PM sees rollout timelines), 2) predictive route tiles show likelihood of navigation targets based on past usage and SLA/alert state, 3) cost-lens microcards surface per-route/token economics inline on relevant tiles, 4) fast keyboard navigation and minimal click flows for common flows (new rollout, create dedicated pool, run eval). This ticket covers ideation, mid-fidelity prototype, usability review, and design handoff artifacts for engineering. Note: this approach intentionally consolidates entry points rather than proliferating top-level nav items, trading discoverability for speed and context—mitigations include an exploratory 'All destinations' overlay and progressive reveal for new users.
acceptance_criteria: Landing zones render a role-aware primary tile and four predictive tiles within 120ms on desktop in staging
Workspace switch action completes and loads associated dashboard in <=2 clicks from primary tile
Cost-lens microcard shows token breakdown (model, prompt vs. generation) and 7-day trend for the selected route
Rollout tile includes actions: 'Create canary', 'View rollout history', 'Rollback' and triggers the existing rollouts API (integration tested)
Prototype usability test with 6 engineers + 4 PMs yields median task completion time improvement >= 25% vs current baseline
comments: 2025-02-14 Marco Liu: Initial problem framing and sketch dump attached to the PRD. Focused on reducing cognitive load for multi-tenant users. Asked Eng for feasibility check on lazy-loading tiles and cost-lens aggregation.

2025-02-18 Aisha Patel: Early mid-fidelity screens posted. Requested to add keyboard-first pattern and accessible focus states. Noted accessibility checklist item for screenreader labels on predictive tiles.

2025-02-21 Engineering sync (Lina Gomez): Eng flagged potential performance impact when pulling cost telemetry for every tile. Action: implement backend aggregation and cache TTL; ENG-4112 added as dependency.

2025-02-25 PM review (Jordan Blake): Suggest surfaced callout for 'Active incidents' to temporarily boost related tiles' weight in predictive scoring. Agreed to add ephemeral prioritization rule and measure false positives.

2025-02-28 Usability session: 6 engineers + 4 PMs tested flows. Findings: predictive tiles useful, but users misinterpreted the canary quick-action (confused about safe defaults). Action: add confirmation + visibility of default traffic %, update microcopy.

2025-03-01 Design iteration: Updated microcard to include a one-line cost delta compared to last week and a tooltip explaining token breakdown. Pushed revised Figma link and asked Eng to review UI components.

2025-03-03 Handoff prep: Annotated components and accessibility notes uploaded. Linked GH PR for initial component shell. Requesting Eng review and estimate for integration work and telemetry endpoints.
Follow-ups: schedule A/B pilot for 2 weeks post-launch to measure task completion and switch latency. If KPI regressions appear, enable roll-back to the original home surface via feature flag.
decision_log: Use role-aware primary tile + up to 4 predictive tiles instead of adding new top-level nav items (decision date: 2025-02-16)
Predictive scoring will combine recency, SLO breaches, and manual pinning — privacy-safe and computed on server (decision date: 2025-02-20)
Cost-lens will show aggregated token buckets rather than full raw logs to avoid heavy reads; link to cost analytics for deep dives (decision date: 2025-02-21)
Rollout quick-action will default to a conservative canary traffic % (5%) and require a confirmation modal to reduce accidental traffic shifts (decision date: 2025-02-28)
risks: Exposing cost information inline could increase telemetry load and cause higher latency if not aggregated; mitigation: server-side TTL cache and rate limit fetches
Users may not discover deeper destinations when primary tiles dominate; mitigation: 'All destinations' overlay and onboarding hints
Predictive ranking could surface noisy items during incidents; mitigation: ephemeral weighting with cooldown and manual pinning override
